title: Galatians Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Galatians chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Galatians Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Galatians Chapter 3.

questions.question: In Galatians 3, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you
Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law
Even as Abraham believed God
Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you
questions.explanation: This event is mentioned first in Galatians 3:1, where Paul addresses the Galatians about their understanding of Christ's crucifixion.

questions.question: What does Paul ask the Galatians regarding how they received the Spirit?
options: By the works of the law
By the hearing of faith
By both works and faith
By their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: By the works of the law
questions.explanation: In Galatians 3:2, Paul inquires whether the Galatians received the Spirit by the works of the law or by the hearing of faith.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:3, what does Paul question about the Galatians' understanding?
options: They began in the flesh
They began in the Spirit
They are wise
They are blessed
questions.correctAnswer: They began in the Spirit
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:3 indicates that Paul asks if they, having begun in the Spirit, are now trying to be made perfect by the flesh.

questions.question: What does Paul imply about the suffering of the Galatians in Galatians 3:4?
options: It was all for a purpose
It may have been in vain
It strengthened their faith
It was necessary
questions.correctAnswer: It may have been in vain
questions.explanation: In Galatians 3:4, Paul questions if they have suffered many things in vain, suggesting uncertainty about their efforts.

questions.question: Who is said to minister the Spirit and work miracles among the Galatians?
options: Paul
Abraham
Jesus
The law
questions.correctAnswer: Paul
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:5 speaks about the one who ministers the Spirit and works miracles among them, which is Paul himself.

questions.question: What was accounted to Abraham for righteousness according to Galatians 3:6?
options: His works
His faith
His sacrifices
His lineage
questions.correctAnswer: His faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:6 states that Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness, emphasizing faith.

questions.question: Who are considered the children of Abraham according to Galatians 3:7?
options: Those who follow the law
Those who are of faith
Those who are circumcised
Those who are Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Those who are of faith
questions.explanation: According to Galatians 3:7, those who are of faith are recognized as the children of Abraham.

questions.question: What does the scripture foresee according to Galatians 3:8?
options: God would justify the heathen through faith
The coming of the law
The end of sacrifices
Abraham's descendants
questions.correctAnswer: God would justify the heathen through faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:8 states that the scripture foresaw that God would justify the heathen through faith and preached the gospel unto Abraham.

questions.question: What blessing do those of faith receive according to Galatians 3:9?
options: A curse
The law
Blessings with faithful Abraham
Miracles
questions.correctAnswer: Blessings with faithful Abraham
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:9 indicates that those who are of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

questions.question: What is said about those who are of the works of the law in Galatians 3:10?
options: They are blessed
They are justified
They are under the curse
They are righteous
questions.correctAnswer: They are under the curse
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:10 states that as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse, highlighting the consequences of relying on the law.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:1, who has bewitched the Galatians?
options: Jesus
The law
A false teacher
Unknown
questions.correctAnswer: Unknown
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:1 questions who has bewitched the Galatians, but does not specify a name, hence it is 'Unknown'.

questions.question: In Galatians 3:4, Paul questions if their suffering was in vain. What does he imply?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Paul implies their suffering could be in vain in Galatians 3:4, highlighting concern for their faith.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:6, Abraham's belief was counted as righteousness. Is this statement true?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:6 clearly states that Abraham's belief in God was accounted to him for righteousness.

questions.question: Galatians 3:10 states that everyone is under the curse of the law. Is this statement true?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:10 specifies that only those who are of the works of the law are under the curse, not everyone.

questions.question: In Galatians 3:8, it is stated that God would justify the Jews through faith. Is this statement true?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:8 states that God would justify the heathen through faith, not specifically the Jews.

medium.title: Galatians Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Galatians Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:11, how is a person justified in the sight of God?
options: By obeying the law
By faith
By works
By rituals
questions.correctAnswer: By faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:11 states that no man is justified by the law but that the just shall live by faith.

questions.question: What does Galatians 3:12 promise will happen if someone does what Galatians 3:11 commands?
options: They shall be cursed
They shall live in the law
They shall receive the Spirit
They shall be justified by works
questions.correctAnswer: They shall live in the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:12 follows 3:11 and says the man that doeth the law shall live in them, contrasting living by faith with living by law.

questions.question: What is the significance of Christ being made a curse for us as described in Galatians 3:13?
options: He fulfilled the law perfectly
He redeemed us from the curse of the law
He established a new law
He became a mediator between God and man
questions.correctAnswer: He redeemed us from the curse of the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:13 explains that Christ was made a curse for us to redeem us from the curse of the law.

questions.question: How does Galatians 3:14 relate the blessing of Abraham to the Gentiles?
options: The blessing of Abraham is only for Jews
The blessing comes through Jesus Christ to the Gentiles
The Gentiles must follow the law to receive the blessing
The blessing is conditional on works
questions.correctAnswer: The blessing comes through Jesus Christ to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:14 states the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What does Galatians 3:15 teach about the nature of a confirmed covenant?
options: It can be easily changed
No one can annul or add to it once confirmed
It applies only to the law
It is only valid for a short time
questions.correctAnswer: No one can annul or add to it once confirmed
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:15 explains that once a man’s covenant is confirmed, no one can annul or add to it.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:16, to whom was the promise originally made?
options: To many seeds
To Abraham’s seed, which is Christ
To the law-keepers
To the angels
questions.correctAnswer: To Abraham’s seed, which is Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:16 states the promises were made to Abraham’s seed, which is Christ, not to many seeds.

questions.question: Why does Galatians 3:17 say the law cannot disannul the promise made to Abraham?
options: Because the law is stronger than the promise
Because the promise was confirmed before the law was given
Because the law was given by angels
Because the law is of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Because the promise was confirmed before the law was given
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:17 explains the promise was confirmed before the law came 430 years later, so the law cannot annul it.

questions.question: What does Galatians 3:18 say about the source of the inheritance?
options: The inheritance comes by the law
The inheritance is no longer of promise
The inheritance was given to Abraham by promise
The inheritance is earned by works
questions.correctAnswer: The inheritance was given to Abraham by promise
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:18 states that the inheritance is not of the law but was given to Abraham by promise.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:19, why was the law added?
options: To make the promise effective
Because of transgressions until the seed should come
To replace the covenant with Abraham
To establish faith
questions.correctAnswer: Because of transgressions until the seed should come
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:19 explains the law was added because of transgressions until the seed to whom the promise was made came.

questions.question: What role does Galatians 3:20 assign to a mediator?
options: A mediator is one between many
God is one and a mediator is not of one
A mediator is unnecessary
A mediator represents only the law
questions.correctAnswer: God is one and a mediator is not of one
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:20 states that a mediator is not mediator of one, but God is one.

questions.question: How does Galatians 3:13 explain the curse of the law is removed from believers practically?
options: By perfect law-keeping
By Christ being made a curse for us
By following rituals
By receiving the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: By Christ being made a curse for us
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:13 teaches that Christ took on the curse by being made a curse for us, redeeming us from it.

questions.question: What practical result does Galatians 3:14 say comes from the blessing of Abraham through Jesus Christ?
options: Receiving the promise of the Spirit through faith
Being justified by the law
Living under the curse
Being sons of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving the promise of the Spirit through faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:14 says the blessing of Abraham comes so we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:11-12, what is the difference between living by faith and living by the law?
options: Living by faith brings curse, living by law brings blessing
Living by faith justifies, living by law requires perfect obedience
Living by faith is impossible, living by law is easy
Living by faith is through works, living by law is through grace
questions.correctAnswer: Living by faith justifies, living by law requires perfect obedience
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:11-12 contrasts justification by faith with the law requiring perfect obedience to live in it.

questions.question: True or False: According to Galatians 3:6-7, those who have faith are considered children of Abraham.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:7 states that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 3:19 says the law was added to replace the promise made to Abraham.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:19 says the law was added because of transgressions until the seed should come, not to replace the promise.

hard.title: Galatians Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Galatians Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:21, why is the law not against the promises of God?
options: Because if there had been a law given which could have given life, righteousness would be by the law
Because the law was given to Abraham
Because the law was added after faith came
Because the law is a schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Because if there had been a law given which could have given life, righteousness would be by the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:21 states that the law is not against the promises of God because if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would indeed come by the law.

questions.question: What does Galatians 3:22 say the scripture has done to all?
options: Concluded all under sin
Set them free from the law
Made them children of God
Given them the promise of the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Concluded all under sin
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:22 explains that scripture has concluded all under sin so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to believers.

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:23, what was the purpose of being kept under the law before faith came?
options: To be shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed
To gain righteousness by works
To receive the Spirit
To be justified by the law
questions.correctAnswer: To be shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:23 states that before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith that would later be revealed.

questions.question: What role does Galatians 3:24 assign to the law?
options: A schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ
A covenant of works
A means to achieve righteousness
A mediator between God and man
questions.correctAnswer: A schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:24 describes the law as our schoolmaster, leading us to Christ so that we may be justified by faith.

questions.question: After faith has come, what does Galatians 3:25 say about our relationship to the law as a schoolmaster?
options: We are no longer under a schoolmaster
We must follow the law more strictly
We remain under the law until the promise is fulfilled
We are under a new schoolmaster
questions.correctAnswer: We are no longer under a schoolmaster
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:25 clearly states that after faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster (the law).

questions.question: According to Galatians 3:28, what unifies believers in Christ Jesus?
options: There is neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, male nor female; for all are one in Christ Jesus
Believers must follow the law equally
Only Jews can inherit the promises
Faith in the law is what unites all
questions.correctAnswer: There is neither Jew nor Greek, bond nor free, male nor female; for all are one in Christ Jesus
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:28 emphasizes the unity of all believers regardless of ethnicity, social status, or gender, stating they are all one in Christ Jesus.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'paidion' in Galatians 3:26 mean?
options: Children
Servants
Teachers
Heirs
questions.correctAnswer: Children
questions.explanation: In Galatians 3:26, 'paidion' (παιδίον) is the Greek word translated as 'children,' referring to believers being children of God by faith.

questions.question: Which literary technique is primarily used in Galatians 3:28 to emphasize unity among believers?
options: Parallelism
Chiasm
Metaphor
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:28 uses parallelism, listing contrasting pairs (Jew/Greek, bond/free, male/female) to emphasize the unity of believers in Christ.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with Galatians 3:6 about Abraham's faith being counted as righteousness?
options: Genesis 15:6
Leviticus 19:18
Exodus 20:12
Deuteronomy 6:4
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 15:6
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:6 references Abraham believing God, which is originally found in Genesis 15:6 where Abraham's faith was counted as righteousness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of unity in Galatians 3:28?
options: Colossians 3:11
Romans 12:2
1 Corinthians 13:1
Ephesians 6:12
questions.correctAnswer: Colossians 3:11
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:11 echoes the theme of unity found in Galatians 3:28, stating there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free, but Christ is all and in all.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Galatians 3:21 in the chapter?
options: Galatians 3:20, discussing the nature of a mediator
Galatians 3:22, about scripture concluding all under sin
Galatians 3:19, about the law being added because of transgressions
Galatians 3:23, about being kept under the law before faith
questions.correctAnswer: Galatians 3:20, discussing the nature of a mediator
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:20 immediately precedes 3:21 and discusses that a mediator is not of one, but God is one, setting up the argument about the law and promises.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of the law as a 'schoolmaster' in Galatians 3:24?
options: The law foreshadows Christ as the one who brings justification by faith
The law is an eternal covenant to be followed strictly
The law is a replacement for faith
The law is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: The law foreshadows Christ as the one who brings justification by faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:24 uses the term 'schoolmaster' (Greek: paidagogos) typologically to show the law's role as a guardian that leads to Christ, who justifies by faith.

questions.question: How does Galatians 3:13 use Old Testament scripture to explain Christ's redemptive role?
options: It quotes Deuteronomy 21:23 about being cursed if hung on a tree
It references Psalm 23 about the shepherd
It cites Isaiah 53 about the suffering servant
It mentions Exodus 12 about the Passover lamb
questions.correctAnswer: It quotes Deuteronomy 21:23 about being cursed if hung on a tree
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:13 refers to Deuteronomy 21:23 to explain that Christ became a curse for us by being hung on a tree, redeeming us from the curse of the law.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 3:26 teaches that all believers are children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:26 explicitly states that 'ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus,' confirming this truth.

questions.question: True or False: Galatians 3:25 teaches that after faith comes, believers remain under the law as a schoolmaster.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:25 states the opposite: 'But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster,' indicating believers are freed from the law as guardian.

theological.title: Galatians Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Galatians Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 3:6 teach about justification?
options: Justification is by faith as exemplified by Abraham
Justification is through perfect obedience to the law
Justification is granted by ritual sacrifice
Justification is based on ethnic descent from Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: Justification is by faith as exemplified by Abraham
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:6 states 'Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness,' teaching that justification comes through faith, not works or lineage.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 3:10 teach regarding the law and the curse?
options: Those who rely on works of the law are under a curse
The law blesses those who keep it perfectly
The law is a means to obtain justification
The curse is lifted by strict law-keeping
questions.correctAnswer: Those who rely on works of the law are under a curse
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:10 says, 'For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse,' indicating reliance on law works results in curse, not blessing.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 3:13 teach about Christ's redemptive work?
options: Christ redeemed us by becoming a curse for us
Christ fulfilled the law so we could keep it perfectly
Christ abolished the law entirely
Christ's redemption is based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: Christ redeemed us by becoming a curse for us
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:13 states, 'Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us,' emphasizing substitutionary atonement.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 3:15 specifically demonstrate?
options: Covenant faithfulness
Omniscience
Justice
Omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:15 discusses the irrevocability of a confirmed covenant, highlighting God's covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 3:21 specifically demonstrate?
options: Holiness
Sovereignty
Justice
Grace
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:21 explains that the law cannot give life or righteousness, showing God's justice in requiring faith rather than law-keeping.

questions.question: How does Galatians 3:24 connect to the broader biblical theme of Christ as mediator?
options: The law acts as a schoolmaster leading to Christ for justification by faith
The law is replaced by the law of Moses
Faith is unnecessary after the law is given
Justification is by works through the law
questions.correctAnswer: The law acts as a schoolmaster leading to Christ for justification by faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:24 describes the law as a guardian until Christ came, connecting to the theme of Christ as mediator leading to salvation by faith.

questions.question: How does Galatians 3:16 relate to the Messianic promise in redemptive history?
options: The promise to Abraham's seed refers specifically to Christ
The promise was only for Abraham's physical descendants
The promise was nullified by the law
The promise was conditional on law obedience
questions.correctAnswer: The promise to Abraham's seed refers specifically to Christ
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:16 clarifies that 'thy seed' is singular and refers to Christ, fulfilling the Messianic promise to Abraham.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 3:23 and 3:25 teach about the law and faith?
options: The law was a temporary guardian until faith came, after which believers are no longer under it
Faith is a replacement for the law but believers remain under legal obligation
The law and faith operate simultaneously as equal means of salvation
The law is abolished and faith is optional
questions.correctAnswer: The law was a temporary guardian until faith came, after which believers are no longer under it
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:23 states we were kept under the law until faith was revealed, and 3:25 confirms that after faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster (the law).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 3:7 and 3:29 teach about believers' identity?
options: Those who have faith are children of Abraham and heirs according to the promise
Only physical descendants of Abraham are heirs
Believers are separated by ethnic distinctions
Faith excludes Gentiles from Abraham's promise
questions.correctAnswer: Those who have faith are children of Abraham and heirs according to the promise
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:7 states that those of faith are Abraham's children, and 3:29 says if you belong to Christ, you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 3:2 and 3:5 teach about the role of faith in receiving the Spirit?
options: The Spirit is received by hearing and believing faith, not by works of the law
The Spirit is granted to those who perfectly keep the law
Works of the law are necessary to receive the Spirit
The Spirit is given only through ritual ceremonies
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit is received by hearing and believing faith, not by works of the law
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:2 and 3:5 both emphasize that the Spirit and miracles come by hearing faith, not by law works.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Galatians 3:11-12 contradicts faith-based justification by teaching law-keeping is necessary. What does Galatians 3:11-12 actually teach?
options: No one is justified by the law; the just live by faith
Righteousness is earned through law-keeping
Faith is subordinate to law obedience
Law and faith together justify a person
questions.correctAnswer: No one is justified by the law; the just live by faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:11 clearly states no one is justified before God by the law, citing 'The just shall live by faith,' while verse 12 explains the law is not based on faith.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 3:8 teach about the inclusion of Gentiles in God's plan?
options: God would justify the Gentiles through faith as foretold to Abraham
The Gentiles are excluded from God's promises
The law was given to justify Gentiles
Gentiles must become Jews to be blessed
questions.correctAnswer: God would justify the Gentiles through faith as foretold to Abraham
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:8 explains that Scripture foresaw God justifying Gentiles by faith and preached this gospel to Abraham, promising blessing to all nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Galatians 3:20 specifically demonstrate?
options: Unity
Wrath
Jealousy
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Unity
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:20 states that God is one and not a mediator of one, emphasizing God's unity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Galatians 3:13 and 3:14 teach about Christ's redemptive purpose?
options: Christ redeemed us from the curse so that Gentiles might receive the blessing of Abraham and the Spirit by faith
Christ abolished all promises to Abraham
Christ's death nullified the law and the promise
The Spirit is given only to Jews
questions.correctAnswer: Christ redeemed us from the curse so that Gentiles might receive the blessing of Abraham and the Spirit by faith
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:13 says Christ redeemed us from the curse by becoming a curse, and 3:14 explains this was so the blessing of Abraham might come to Gentiles through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What doctrine does Galatians 3:19 teach about the purpose of the law?
options: The law was added because of transgressions until the promised seed came
The law provides eternal life
The law and promise are the same
The law was given to abolish the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: The law was added because of transgressions until the promised seed came
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:19 states that the law was added on account of transgressions and was temporary until the coming of the promised seed (Christ).
